chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Hakim, the mu'adhdhin of Banu Abs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'And know that whatever you gain from spoils, one-fifth is for Allah and for the Messenger.' He said, 'It is, by Allah, the benefit/profit day by day, except that my father (peace be upon him) made our Shia exempt from that portion of it, so that they may purify themselves.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of khums as a daily benefit and how was it applied to the Shia?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the term 'khums' in the context of spoils as the daily benefit or profit derived from wealth, linking it to the concept of *al-ifadah*. He notes that his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), granted an exemption for the Shia from this specific deduction to ensure their wealth was purified (*li-yazkū*), reflecting a practical application of divine law to facilitate the community's economic stability and spiritual growth.
